pages.text:
The peaches in Wukong’s backyard are
ripe and sweet.
Today he picked a big pile of them from
the trees at the back of the yard.
The peaches sit on a picnic mat like a
little hill.
Wukong wants to share them with
his neighbors.
2

While Wukong looks at the pile, a new
friend walks into the backyard.
He is Bull King, a round little bull with
two short horns and a small gold crown.
“Need a hand?” he asks.
“Do we have enough peaches for
every neighbor?”
3

Wukong starts to count, and he touches
each peach with his finger.
When he gets to twenty-six, one peach
rolls off the mat.
He runs after it and puts it back.
Now he cannot remember where he
stopped, so he starts again.
4

The second time, Wukong counts
thirty-one peaches.
The third time, he counts thirty-six.
“I counted three times and got three
different numbers!” he says, and he flops
down on the grass.
The pile is too big to count one by one.
5

“I can grab lots with my big hands!” says
Bull King.
His first handful has seven, and he puts
them in a heap.
His second handful has only five.
One handful is big and one is small, so
handfuls do not help them count.
6

Then Bull King grabs a third, really
big handful.
Two peaches slip out between his fingers
and roll into the grass.
He picks them up and puts every peach
back on the mat.
Then he scratches his horn and says,
“Show me, please.”
7

Sandy comes over with a stack of paper
bags that are all the same size.
“A handful can be big or small,” he says,
“but each bag holds just ten.”
Wukong will count, and Bull King will put
the peaches in.
8

Wukong counts out loud, and Bull King
puts in one peach at a time.
He is very gentle with his big hands.
At ten, Bull King folds the top of the bag.
Sandy draws a big 10 on it, so everyone
can see it is full.
9

They fill a second bag and then a third
bag in the same way.
Now three full bags stand in a row next
to the mat.
Only four peaches are left over, so they
cannot fill another bag.
10

Bull King points at the bags and then at
the peaches.
“That is three tens and four ones,”
he says.
Sandy writes 34 on a little card.
“The three is for the three bags,” he
says, “and the four is for the four
peaches left over.”
11

Now they count by tens, and it is
much faster.
Wukong taps each bag, and Bull King taps
each peach.
Together they shout, “Ten, twenty, thirty,
thirty-one, thirty-two,
thirty-three, thirty-four!”
Nobody loses count this time.
12

When Bull King walks by the far peach
trees, he spots more peaches in the grass.
He brings back six and sets them down
gently next to the four.
“Four and six make ten,” says Wukong.
“That is enough for one more bag!”
13

Bull King fills the fourth bag while
Wukong counts all the way to ten.
Now there are four full bags and no
peaches left on the mat.
Sandy turns the card over and writes 40.
“Four tens make forty!” says Bull
King proudly.
14

Now they can give the peaches away, one
bag for each neighbor.
They do not need to count again, because
every bag holds ten.
Pigsy lives next door, so the first bag
goes to him over the low fence.
15

Then Wukong and Bull King carry the
other three bags to more neighbors.
Bull King holds one bag in each hand, and
he walks slowly and steadily.
Not one peach gets squashed.
“Strong hands can be gentle hands, too,”
says Bull King with a smile.
16
